options.title: How did Russia get so big?
options.first_line: How did Russia get so big? It once stopped at these mountains, the Urals.
options.first_frame: The old map of northern Asia with Russia's huge shape tracing itself in light from the Baltic to the Pacific, then shrinking back to a small patch west of the Ural Mountains.

options.title: Russia once ended at the Urals. Then what?
options.first_line: Russia once ended at the Ural Mountains. So how did it reach the Pacific?
options.first_frame: A small red Russia west of a brown mountain ridge on the map, a Cossack boat already rowing east off the edge of it into empty forest.

options.title: Why is Russia this huge?
options.first_line: Russia is the biggest country on the map. Why is it this huge?
options.first_frame: Russia's whole shape lit red across the top of the world map, every other country pale beside it, the camera slowly pulling back to show its full width.

why: It names Russia and gives a fact you can picture (it once ended at the Urals) that sets up a real question with the answer held back (how did it reach the Pacific?), and its first frame of a small Russia and a Cossack boat rowing into empty forest tells the mystery even with the sound off.
